official.deadline_note: There is no scholarship application deadline because you cannot apply for this fellowship. The University of Groningen Admission Office nominates candidates, and only applicants holding a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February can be considered. To leave time for the Admission Office to process the application, the master application should be completed before 1 December.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle tied to master's admission for a September start: master application completed before 1 December, provisional or unconditional admission offer received before February, nomination by the Admission Office
official.status_note: The fellowship is nomination-based with no application window: the page states it is not possible to actively apply and that suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination. The master admission cycle itself remains open, with applications to be completed before 1 December for a September start.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "The grant covers tuition fee, costs of international travel, subsistence, books, and health insurance." The grant is awarded for 1-year or 2-year Master's degree programmes starting in September only.
benefits: Tuition fee for the master programme
eligibility: Have received provisional or unconditional admission for a master programme before February, since only then will applicants be considered for a grant
Have excellent academic performance, preferably to be confirmed by letters of recommendation
Have excellent grades during your bachelor or undergraduate studies
Have excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the programme of choice
Be available for the whole period of the programme and be able to take part in the entire programme
Be in good health, so that health insurance in the Netherlands can be arranged
Hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1 of the fellowship
Have no other means of financing the study in question
requirements: Apply for admission to a University of Groningen master programme through the normal route; there is no separate scholarship application
Complete the master application before 1 December so that a provisional or unconditional offer can be received before February
Hold the nationality of a country listed in Appendix 1 of the fellowship
selection_criteria: Excellent academic performance and excellent undergraduate grades, preferably confirmed by letters of recommendation
Excellent English language proficiency in accordance with the admission requirements of the programme of choice

The University of Groningen Admission Office, in consultation with the Admission Boards of the faculties, determines which applicants are nominated; a considerable number of students apply each year while only a limited number of grants can be issued
application_method: Apply for admission to a University of Groningen master programme through the normal admission route
Ensure the master application is completed before 1 December so that a provisional or unconditional admission offer is received before February
Be nominated by the University of Groningen Admission Office, in consultation with the Admission Boards of the faculties; suitable candidates are informed about a nomination
official.application_route: There is no application: apply for a University of Groningen master programme through the normal admission route and be nominated by the Admission Office once you hold a provisional or unconditional offer received before February.
official.study_mode: Full-time master programme, 1 year or 2 years, starting in September only
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1 of the fellowship; residency is not a stated criterion
official.international_eligibility: Yes - restricted to nationals of the countries listed in Appendix 1 of the fellowship
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All master programmes are eligible ('Programmes: All'), but only programmes starting in September; February and April starts are not eligible
official.duration: 1 year or 2 years Master's degree programme, starting in September only
official.description: The Eric Bleumink Fellowship is a University of Groningen grant for nationals of the countries listed in Appendix 1, covering tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance for a one- or two-year master programme starting in September. It is nomination-based, so there is no direct scholarship application.
official.english_requirement: Excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the programme of choice; no separate score is specified for the fellowship itself

not_confirmed: funding_amount, funding_currency, funding_period - the University of Groningen publishes no euro value for the tuition, subsistence, travel, books or insurance components
deadline_central - the page states it is not possible to actively apply, so no application deadline exists; only the master admission timing of before 1 December and before February is published
documents - no document list is published for the fellowship, since nomination follows the master admission application rather than a separate submission
verification.notes: Eligibility criteria, coverage items, the nomination route, the Appendix 1 country requirement and the September-only start rule were read directly from the University of Groningen's Eric Bleumink Fellowship page (page last modified 11 August 2026).

applicant_utility.summary: You never apply for this fellowship, so the only lever you control is the timetable of your master application: it has to be finished before 1 December so that a provisional or unconditional offer reaches you before February, because the Admission Office will not consider anyone who receives their offer later. This also means the award cannot be rescued by a strong late application or a well-argued appeal - if you are not in the nomination pipeline by February, the cycle is effectively over for you. Check Appendix 1 against your nationality rather than your residence, and note that the fellowship only funds programmes that start in September.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nationals of an Appendix 1 country with excellent undergraduate grades, who are applying to a University of Groningen master programme with a September start and who have no other way to finance the degree.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the Appendix 1 country list against your nationality before anything else, since the fellowship is nationality-based
Complete the master application well before 1 December, not merely near it, so the offer arrives before February
Secure strong letters of recommendation with the admission application, since academic performance should preferably be confirmed by them
Confirm your chosen programme starts in September, and choose another funding route if it starts in February or April
Be able to show you have no other means of financing the study, since this is an explicit eligibility condition
Plan for Dutch health insurance arrangements, since being in good health so insurance can be arranged is a stated condition
common_rejection_risks: Completing the master application in January and receiving the offer after February, which removes you from nomination despite strong grades
Applying to a programme with a February or April start, which the fellowship does not fund
Holding a nationality that is not on the Appendix 1 list, or confusing residence or previous study with nationality
Being unable to attend the whole programme, since availability for the entire period is a stated criterion
Having another funding source, since applicants must have no other means of financing the study
A limited number of grants against a considerable number of applicants, so strong but not exceptional grades may simply not be nominated
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published grant covers tuition, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance, but no euro amounts are given, so treat the subsistence component as a contribution and plan personally for relocation, visa costs, furnishings and any programme-specific materials.
document_audit: There is no scholarship document set: the nomination is decided from your master application file, so transcripts and recommendation letters uploaded for admission are your application
Because letters of recommendation are named as the preferred confirmation of academic performance, a file with no referee statement weakens the nomination
The fellowship page links to a separate 'applying for the grant' page and to the Eric Bleumink Fund for more detail, so check both for any programme-specific instructions
Your master application must be complete before 1 December, which means including any documents the programme requires, not just registering an intent
alerts: You cannot apply, so do not wait for a scholarship round that will never open; the effective deadline is the master admission deadline of before 1 December
The University of Groningen awards only a limited number of grants each year against considerable demand, so this is competitive by design
Only programmes starting in September are eligible, which rules out the February and April intakes
Nationality must be on the Appendix 1 list; check the published list rather than assuming a region qualifies
Nomination is decided by the Admission Office with the faculty Admission Boards, so the programme you apply to affects your chances
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No scholarship submission exists: complete the master application before 1 December, receive a provisional or unconditional offer before February, and wait for a nomination decision by the Admission Office in consultation with the faculty Admission Boards.
